chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, who said:

I said to Abu Ibrahim Musa (peace be upon him): A man married a woman but died before consummating the marriage with her; is she permissible for his son? He said: 'They dislike it because he acquired the contract.'

And whenever a man acquires a girl, and he touches her or looks at her in a way that is not permissible for others to look at her, with desire, she becomes forbidden to his father and his son in all cases.
What indicates this is what he narrated:

key_terms.مَلَكَ الْعُقْدَةَ: Acquired the contract (marriage bond without consummation)

ai.seo_question: Is a woman forbidden to her husband's son if he dies before consummating the marriage?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) clarifies the Shia juristic distinction between mere contractual acquisition (malak al-'aqd) and actual possession (malak al-yad) regarding the prohibition of a deceased father's wife to his son. While the majority of scholars (Ahl al-Sunnah) consider the contract sufficient for prohibition, the Imam explains that the stricter prohibition for both father and son applies when there is physical intimacy or lustful gaze, highlighting the nuance between the 'contract' and the 'possession' in marital law.
